claims.text: MnNiSi-based alloys have an inherently large magnetocaloric effect.
The baseline MnNiSi-based alloy has limited fracture toughness.
The baseline MnNiSi-based alloy has limited yield strength.
Warm rolling near 400°C, intermediate tempering near 350°C, and rapid water quenching will refine the grain structure of MnNiSi-based alloys.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will improve mechanical properties without significantly altering the magnetocaloric transition.
Warm rolling near 400°C induces plastic deformation.
The treatment will enhance subgrain formation and produce a uniformly refined microstructure.
The treatment will create controlled dislocation networks while maintaining magnetic phase-boundary integrity.
Dislocation networks introduced by warm rolling act as barriers to crack propagation.
Intermediate tempering near 350°C promotes stress relaxation.
Intermediate tempering near 350°C stabilizes the magnetic phases.
Rapid quenching locks in the refined microstructure while avoiding diffusion sufficient to shift the magnetic transition temperatures.
The treated alloy will have greater fracture toughness than the conventionally processed baseline.
The treated alloy will have greater yield strength than the conventionally processed baseline.
The treated alloy will have greater fatigue resistance than the conventionally processed baseline.
The treated alloy's magnetocaloric transition temperature will remain essentially unchanged relative to the baseline.
The treated alloy's magnetocaloric entropy change will remain essentially unchanged relative to the baseline.
Mechanical and magnetocaloric outcomes depend sensitively on rolling temperature, tempering temperature and duration, and quenching rate.
